chunks: And say: 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'And say: My Lord, forgive and have mercy' in Surah Al-Mu'minun?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as the concluding du'a of Surah Al-Mu'minun, highlighting the Prophet's role as the perfect intercessor and the believer's reliance on divine mercy over their own deeds. The phrase 'Khayr al-Rahimin' (Best of the Merciful) is interpreted to mean that while other beings may show mercy, God's mercy is the ultimate source and perfection of all merciful acts. This reinforces the theological concept of Tawhid in attributes, where all divine qualities are rooted in His essence.
